sources.authors: Michèle B. Nuijten, Chris H. J. Hartgerink, Marcel A. L. M. van Assen, Sacha Epskamp, Jelte M. Wicherts
sources.title: The prevalence of statistical reporting errors in psychology (1985–2013)
sources.what_was_read: the abstract, in full, on the PubMed Central record
quotes: This study documents reporting errors in a sample of over 250,000 p-values reported in eight major psychology journals from 1985 until 2013
half of all published psychology papers that use NHST contained at least one p-value that was inconsistent with its test statistic and degrees of freedom
One in eight papers contained a grossly inconsistent p-value that may have affected the statistical conclusion
sources.why_it_is_here: The established method this session's consistency check is a cousin of: recompute a reported statistic from the numbers printed beside it. No novelty of method is claimed against it.
sources.caveat: The journal and year line as rendered by the fetch was not separately verified character for character; the identifier PMC5101263 and the quoted abstract sentences are what this session read.

sources.authors: Nicholas J. L. Brown, James A. J. Heathers
sources.title: The GRIM Test: A Simple Technique Detects Numerous Anomalies in the Reporting of Results in Psychology
sources.journal: Social Psychological and Personality Science, 2017, volume 8
sources.what_was_read: the abstract, in full, on the institutional record page
quotes: We tested this technique with a sample of 260 recent empirical articles in leading journals.

Of the articles that we could test with the GRIM technique (N = 71), around half (N = 36) appeared to contain at least one inconsistent mean, and more than 20% (N = 16) contained multiple such inconsistencies.
sources.why_it_is_here: The nearest published relative of this session's first measurement. GRIM reports amenability at the ARTICLE level in psychology -- 71 of 260, 27.3 % -- where this session measures it at the CLAIM level in two other literatures. The comparison is offered as a neighbour, not as a baseline: the units differ.
sources.caveat: The preprint at peerj.com/preprints/2064 answered 403 to this session by direct fetch and by a dispatched client; the abstract was read on the institutional record page instead. The full text was not read, and nothing here rests on anything outside the two quoted sentences.
